sanity_expectations: finite and real over the whole S range
unimodal in S: g rises from low/negative values at very low S, peaks at intermediate supply, then declines at high S as co-limitation and inhibition suppress growth
net growth can be negative at very low S where the maintenance drain exceeds uptake
monotone-decelerating growth contribution at low-to-mid S (power-law diminishing returns, 0<b<1)
high-S decline driven jointly by the co-limitation ceiling (strongest near S≈38) and the inhibition factor
excitation_report: σ=0.01 (~0.7% of peak g). Term multiples of σ: growth product term 56.4×; maintenance drain term 6.98×; new co-limitation factor (E−parent) 130× with peak effect 1.30 at S≈37.7. All terms clear the 5×σ visibility bar. Growth and maintenance auto_balance-confirmed; maintenance had no private linear coefficient, so it was made visible by physically raising the floor m (0.2→0.4), the demand scale m_scale (0.02→0.03) and broadening the maintenance threshold S_maint (1.5→3, h=2) so the low-S drain is not diluted, plus tightening σ to 0.01.
role_corrections: g: output->dependent variable (confirmed; explicitly solvable LHS, no derivatives/integrals)
S: input axis->independent variable (confirmed; sole sampling axis, log range 0.1-100)
m: P->P (confirmed; raised to 0.4 for maintenance visibility)
S_maint: P->P (confirmed; raised to 3 to broaden low-S drain)
rationale: Static explicit biological dose-response: g is a closed-form function of the single resource-supply axis S; the remaining 14 symbols are fixed physical parameters (integration dummies absent). Values chosen within the supplied hint ranges (S_colim=20, c_demand=1, d=1, q=3) and physically sensible defaults for the inherited growth/maintenance/inhibition structure. S sampled log-uniformly over [0.1,100] to resolve the low-S maintenance switch (S_maint=3) as well as the mid/high-S half-saturation (S_half=10), co-limitation (peak effect S≈38) and inhibition (S_inhib=60). All terms, and the new co-limitation factor in particular, exceed 5×σ, so no term is hidden under noise.

scenario_text: A population's per-capita growth response is measured across environments with different resource supply rates. Growth rate scales with supply following a decelerating power relationship reflecting diminishing returns of added resources. Experimenters record instantaneous per-capita growth across fixed supply levels. This benchmark targets the scaling of growth performance with resource input.
